This is your private demarkus memory: a personal, versioned markdown store. Your identity maps to exactly one world; call mark_worlds once to learn its name, then address every document as mark://{worldName}/{path}. A project the user names lives under /<slug>/ with the root's layout; otherwise the world root.

Recall first: check this memory before answering recall questions. Prefer scoped lookup (limit 3): catalog for names/tags, match=body for section text or catalog misses. Answer in one section: omit budget, fetch the best returned #anchor. Answer spanning documents or their relations (supersedes, depends on, implements, derives from, influenced by, roles): budget=1500 on the first lookup; cite its '>>>' blocks, fetch a #anchor only for a passage they omit. Path-only results: use match=body or mark_explore to locate a section, or fetch without force for a short body or outline; select a returned anchor if outlined. Never invent anchors; expand only focused evidence. Use your world's URL or an established subtree and descriptive subjects. Your world's index.md is the untagged-content backstop. Never invent memory.

Read outcomes: Primary lookup or document-fetch failure: disclose and stop that operation; never infer absence. Recoverable expansion fetch/section or exploration sibling-listing failures: retain valid tables/cards, disclose gaps and continue from usable results. Partial empty results and body requests answered wholly or partly by catalog are inconclusive; missing body-mode confirmation is catalog fallback. Only a successful, non-partial empty lookup without mode fallback establishes no matches.

Record as you go: write what is worth keeping unasked and name the full path written. Routes under the project root: decisions to adr/<NNNN>-<title>.md (NNNN from mark_list's next:), bug lessons to debugging.md, patterns to patterns.md, session progress through mark_append with route today, plans to plans/<name>.md, reflections to thoughts.md; the rest per /.well-known/demarkus/template.md; unplaceable: ask where. Keep index.md current. Skip trivia; capture the non-obvious.

Update: mark_fetch with force=true, edit, mark_publish at that version with the complete metadata map; never publish an outline. Every mark_publish sets metadata: tags (comma-separated subjects), importance (0-1; 0.8+ for the hub and key decisions), type (Decision, Plan, Journal, Guide, Architecture or Reference; hubs none). No YAML frontmatter in the body; a document's name is its # H1. Never set metadata.retention unless the user explicitly asked; it permanently deletes older versions. No secrets or credentials: the server refuses them.
